title: A Novel Framework Combining MPC and Deep Reinforcement Learning With Application to Freeway Traffic Control

method_nodes.source_quote: Initialize critic and actor networks... Initialize target network... Initialize experience replay buffer R
method_nodes.description: Initialize the DRL agent's actor and critic networks, their corresponding target networks, and the experience replay buffer. This setup prepares the hierarchical framework for training and control.

method_nodes.source_quote: Perform high-level MPC with freeway model F and prediction horizon Np,s, by solving optimization problem (5)-(A.3)
method_nodes.description: The high-level MPC module solves a nonlinear optimization problem at a low frequency (Tc) using a nominal METANET model to generate a baseline control input (ub) that satisfies constraints.
The low-level DRL agent selects an ancillary action (url) at a high frequency (Td) to modify the MPC output. Exploration noise is added during the learning phase.

method_nodes.source_quote: Execute action uc(kd) in the freeway network, with the real traffic demand d(ks)
method_nodes.description: The combined control input is calculated as the saturated sum of the MPC baseline and DRL modification, then applied to the freeway network simulation.

method_nodes.source_quote: Store transition (xrl(kd), url(kd), rt(kd), xrl(kd + 1)) in R
method_nodes.description: Transitions consisting of states, actions, and rewards are collected and stored in the replay buffer to be used for off-policy training of the DRL agent.

method_nodes.source_quote: Update the critic network... Update the actor network... Update the target networks
method_nodes.description: The actor and critic networks are updated using n-step temporal-difference learning and the Adam optimizer. Target networks are slowly updated to maintain stability.

method_nodes.source_quote: The proposed MPC-DRL framework is now implemented and evaluated via a benchmark freeway network
method_nodes.description: The trained framework is evaluated on a benchmark freeway network under various noise scenarios and compared against standalone MPC and DRL methods.

source_nodes.source_quote: The proposed framework is implemented on a benchmark freeway network in order to coordinate ramp metering and variable speed limits
source_nodes.description: A synthetic freeway network consisting of two origins (one mainstream and one on-ramp) and one destination. The main stretch is 6 km long, divided into 6 segments of 1 km each.

sink_nodes.source_quote: Learning performance of standalone DRL and combined MPC-DRL with and without 10-step TD for different scenarios.
sink_nodes.description: Learning curves showing reward over 3000 episodes for standalone DRL and the proposed MPC-DRL framework across six scenarios involving different noise levels and demand profiles.

sink_nodes.source_quote: Comparison of the control performance for different controllers for different scenarios, in terms of TTS, TWT, constraint violation, mean computation time, and max computation time
sink_nodes.description: Quantitative performance metrics (TTS, TWT, speed, constraint violation, and CPU time) for six control strategies across six simulation scenarios.

hyperparameters.name: Learning rate
hyperparameters.source_quote: Learning rate (both actor and critic networks) 0.001

hyperparameters.name: n
hyperparameters.source_quote: n = 10 is chosen for the DRL module
